verdicts.verification_notes: Verified at src/backend/src/index.ts:19 (app.use('*', cors())), src/backend/src/middleware/auth.ts:34-88 (clientHeadersAndAuthMiddleware unconditionally sets DEFAULT_USER_ID on every request), src/backend/src/routes/voice.ts:18-31 (/deepgram/token), 53-83 (/v2/dictation/gemini-token), 169-211 (/realtime/token raw key fallback), and src/backend/src/routes/worker.ts:520-560 (/memory). Also confirmed by live evidence in docs/audit/evidence/ws-c/audit-summary.json (preflightAllowOrigin: '*', memoryReadWithoutAuthOrOriginRestriction: true).

Verified at src/backend/src/middleware/gzip.ts:18-20: await c.req.raw.arrayBuffer() and gunzipSync(compressedBuffer) are called synchronously on the main event loop with no compressed byte limit and no maxOutputLength option. Confirmed by live magnification test in docs/audit/evidence/ws-c/audit-summary.json (15,331 bytes compressed -> 15,728,652 bytes uncompressed, 1,025.9x expansion ratio).

Confirmed that GET /auth/v1/authorize (src/backend/src/routes/auth.ts:100-121) takes an unvalidated redirect_to/redirect_uri query parameter, mints a 1-year access_token, appends it to the URL, and returns a 302 redirect to any external host (leaksTokenToExternalHost: true). Precision refinement: AUD-C-003's description attributed the unvalidated redirect_to HTML link to GET /auth/start (citing lines 76-85); in the actual code, lines 56-94 are GET /auth/callback (which reads unvalidated redirect_to and injects it into both href and window.location.href — see new finding AUD-C-016), whereas GET /auth/start (lines 128-175) constructs location from scheme === 'kursor' ? 'kursor' : 'heyclicky'.

Verified at src/backend/src/routes/auth.ts:27-39 (createLocalJwt hardcodes base64UrlEncode('kursor-local-dev-signature') as the third JWT segment), auth.ts:236-248 (POST /auth/v1/logout deletes from sessions), and src/backend/src/middleware/auth.ts:34-88 (never verifies JWT signature, exp, or sessions table existence). Confirmed in docs/audit/evidence/ws-c/audit-summary.json (revokedTokenStillAcceptedStatus: 200, forgedSignatureJwtAcceptedStatus: 200).

Verified at src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:1021-1045: POST /brain/turn awaits tryCallUpstreamLlm(...) at line 1021 before checking if (upstream && !body.force_local_fallback) at line 1045. Confirmed by docs/audit/evidence/ws-c/test-phase2-stderr.txt showing live Groq calls during force_local_fallback: true tests.

Verified at src/backend/src/test-phase1.ts:155 (hardcodes assert.equal(data.mouth.primary_provider, 'openai-realtime'), failing when .env sets MOUTH_PRIMARY_PROVIDER=gemini-tts) and src/backend/src/routes/voice.ts:263-320 (ensureWarmSynthWorker spawns persistent powershell.exe at module load without .unref(), hanging test-phase1.ts and test-phase2.ts after server.close()).

Verified against src/backend/src/middleware/auth.ts:44-60, src/backend/src/routes/worker.ts:206-340, and C# ClickyClientHeadersHandler.cs / WorkerClient.cs:61 / RegisteredDevice.cs. Backend reads x-clicky-device-id instead of X-Clicky-Device and body.device_name instead of body.display_name, and omits id, display_name, is_this_device, and capabilities required by C# RegisteredDevice.

Verified against src/backend/src/routes/worker.ts:406-485 and C# StarterPlanResponse.cs, StarterPlanClicky.cs, and StarterPlanSuggestion.cs. worker.ts returns { title, prompt, why } for clickys (missing key, name, role, description, intro_messages, reveal_line, first_asks) and { id, title, tagline, initial_prompt, schedule_hint } for suggested_agents (missing description, agent_prompt).

Confirmed that src/backend/src/db/index.ts has zero CREATE INDEX statements, EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows SCAN sessions and SCAN notifications + USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY, sessions grows monotonically without pruning, and ensureSessionAndThread (brain.ts:172-187) stores raw base64 screenshots in threads.messages_json. Precision refinement on column names in remediation: in db/index.ts:78-113, the actual columns are notifications(user_id, is_read, created_at DESC), proactive_cards(user_id, dismissed), and threads(user_id) (threads.id stores sessionId; there is no threads.session_id column).

Verified at src/backend/src/routes/agents.ts:943 (returns proxy_url: 'http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp/composio') and src/backend/src/routes/worker.ts:983, 990 (returns 'http://127.0.0.1:8787/billing/local-max-active' and 'http://127.0.0.1:8787/billing/local-portal'). None of those three routes exist in the backend, returning 404 Not Found.

Verified at src/backend/src/routes/worker.ts:995-1003 (/account/delete and /me/account/delete are pure no-ops that delete 0 rows), worker.ts:1005-1020 (/telemetry/client-error and /report-error discard ErrorReport), worker.ts:1045-1050 (/me/companion-history is a pure no-op returning []), and src/backend/src/routes/agents.ts:929-934, 1112-1173 (/label no-op, /tools/execute-connector stub, /tools/spotify/search hardcoded track).

Verified at src/backend/src/routes/agents.ts:83-85 (proactiveJobs, proactiveCardStatuses), 534 (turnLeases), 711 (integrationsCatalog), and 972 (calendarEvents) — all stored in volatile in-memory Maps/arrays without TTL eviction or SQLite persistence for jobs, leases, integrations, or calendar events.

Confirmed fragile regex scraping in searchDuckDuckGoHtml (worker.ts:620-621) and silent HTTP 200 synthetic fallback (worker.ts:756-766). Precision refinement on decodeHtmlEntities (worker.ts:571-582): .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, '') is on line 580 AFTER .replace(/</g, '<').replace(/>/g, '>') on lines 574-575 (and .replace(/&/g, '&') runs first on line 573). This causes double-unescaping (&lt; -> < -> <) AND causes legitimate decoded angle-bracket text (e.g., 'a < b && c > d' or 'List<string>') to be silently stripped by /<[^>]+>/g.

Verified across auth.ts, worker.ts, brain.ts, and agents.ts: try { body = await c.req.json(); } catch {} silently swallows malformed JSON and falls back to {} with HTTP 200, and PUT/POST /memory (worker.ts:520-553) has no payload size limit.

new_findings.title: GET /auth/callback and GET /callback Allow DOM XSS via Unvalidated javascript: Scheme in redirect_to Parameter
new_findings.description: In handleAuthCallback (GET /auth/callback and GET /callback, src/backend/src/routes/auth.ts:56-94), line 58 reads const redirectTo = c.req.query('redirect_to') || 'heyclicky://auth-callback' without validating the URL protocol or host. Line 60 constructs targetUrl via buildCallbackUrl(redirectTo, { code, state }), and lines 84 and 88 render href="${escapeHtml(targetUrl)}" and <script>window.location.href = ${JSON.stringify(targetUrl)};</script> inside an HTML response served on http://127.0.0.1:8787. Because neither escapeHtml() nor JSON.stringify() blocks the javascript: URI scheme, passing redirect_to=javascript:alert(document.domain)// causes the inline script to immediately execute window.location.href = "javascript:alert(document.domain)//?code=..." in the http://127.0.0.1:8787 origin.
reproduction: 2. Inspect the returned HTML at lines 84 and 88.
new_findings.observed: The response is 200 text/html containing <script>window.location.href = "javascript:fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8787/deepgram/token',{method:'POST'})//?code=...";</script>, which executes arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the local backend origin http://127.0.0.1:8787.
new_findings.expected: Strictly validate redirect_to in handleAuthCallback (and buildCallbackUrl) so only heyclicky://, kursor://, or loopback http://127.0.0.1 / http://localhost URLs are permitted, rejecting javascript:, data:, and external https: schemes with HTTP 400.
new_findings.impact: Same-origin arbitrary JavaScript execution (DOM XSS) on http://127.0.0.1:8787, bypassing even same-origin protections if CORS is restricted.
new_findings.remediation: Validate the parsed URL protocol of redirect_to against an allowlist (['heyclicky:', 'kursor:', 'http:'] with loopback hostname check for http:) before rendering or redirecting in src/backend/src/routes/auth.ts:48-94.

new_findings.title: nextSuggestionNumericId Resets to 101 on Backend Restart and Overwrites/Un-Dismisses Existing proactive_cards Rows in SQLite
new_findings.description: src/backend/src/routes/agents.ts:85 initializes let nextSuggestionNumericId = 101; as an in-memory counter rather than seeding it from SELECT MAX(CAST(id AS INTEGER)) FROM proactive_cards. When createProactiveJob() runs (agents.ts:104-107, 156-175), it assigns IDs '101', '102', etc. and executes INSERT INTO proactive_cards (...) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET title = excluded.title, ..., dismissed = 0. Consequently, after every backend restart, the next proactive job creation reuses IDs 101, 102, ... and overwrites previously stored cards in SQLite, resetting dismissed = 0 on cards the user had already dismissed or resolved.
reproduction: 1. Call POST /proactive/jobs (creates cards 101 and 102) and resolve/dismiss card 101 via POST /proactive/cards/resolve with {card_ids:['101'], resolution:'dismissed'}.
2. Restart the backend server (nextSuggestionNumericId resets to 101) and call POST /proactive/jobs again.
3. Query SELECT id, dismissed, payload_json FROM proactive_cards WHERE id = '101'.
new_findings.observed: Card '101' in SQLite is overwritten and its dismissed column is reset from 1 back to 0 (and status reset to 'presented').
new_findings.expected: Initialize nextSuggestionNumericId from SELECT COALESCE(MAX(CAST(id AS INTEGER)), 100) + 1 FROM proactive_cards at startup (or use a SQLite INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT / UUID).
new_findings.impact: Previously dismissed or resolved proactive suggestion cards reappear as unread/active after a backend restart.
new_findings.remediation: Seed nextSuggestionNumericId from the SQLite proactive_cards table on startup in src/backend/src/routes/agents.ts:85.

new_findings.title: GET /auth/v1/authorize and GET /auth/start Mint Access Tokens Without Inserting Session Rows Into SQLite sessions Table
new_findings.description: While POST /auth/v1/token (src/backend/src/routes/auth.ts:198-207) inserts each minted access_token and refresh_token into the SQLite sessions table, GET /auth/v1/authorize (auth.ts:107-121) and GET /auth/start (auth.ts:131-175) call createLocalJwt(DEFAULT_USER_ID, DEFAULT_EMAIL) and return the minted access_token and refresh_token directly to the caller without inserting a row into SQLite sessions.
reproduction: 2. Call GET /auth/start?format=json and check SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE access_token = <returned_token>.
new_findings.observed: 0 rows exist in SQLite sessions for tokens minted via GET /auth/v1/authorize or GET /auth/start.
new_findings.expected: Every endpoint that mints an access_token and refresh_token must persist the session row in SQLite sessions so session validation, token refresh, and logout work consistently across all auth flows.
new_findings.impact: Inconsistent session state in SQLite; once AUD-C-004 is fixed to validate bearer tokens against the sessions table, tokens obtained via /auth/v1/authorize or /auth/start will be rejected as unknown sessions.
new_findings.remediation: Insert a sessions row in handleAuthorize (auth.ts:107) and handleAuthStart (auth.ts:131) using the same INSERT INTO sessions statement used in handleToken (auth.ts:198-207).
